subject: [Invite] Toronto AI / CV Leaders Community
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Over the last two years, we've hosted intimate roundtable dinners for AI / CV Execs in London, Paris, New York, & SF (see positive feedback here: [LINK]) - & now we're looking to start building a similar community in Toronto. 

My team and I are going to be in town Mon 24th - Tues 25th Feb & we'd love to grab a coffee to get your feedback on what event formats could work well / connect more broadly & swap notes on what we're seeing in the space.

In case you're not familiar with Encord, we're a ~5 years old AI scale up, with 100+ employees & offices in London & San Francisco. 

Would you be interested in having a quick coffee?

subject: Is building your AI models painful?
text:
Hi [NAME] 

Saw you are working as Head of AI at [COMPANY] and we missed you at CES.​

If you spend a significant amount of time using different apps for annotating/labeling, curating/indexing data, and model eval, it may be time to consider an end to end platform like Encord. We have had hundreds of AI teams join us in [YEAR] to either optimize or consolidate their ML team workflows. Saving you time, money, and providing you speed to market. 

Don't become numb to the pain of building your ML workflows because they get you by. Make your life and your teams better God willing by using Encord.

We would love for a quick 30 minutes this week to learn more about your work and the pains you are experiencing in your AI workflows.

subject: AI development costs
text:
Hi [NAME], Navendu,

Been having some productive conversations with Himanshu, Anshuman & the
wider [COMPANY] team, focusing on how we can improve cost efficiencies of
[COMPANY]'s AI development across the organisation.

There's a few areas we've identified that will realise significant cost
efficiencies, whilst improving model performance:

   -
*1) Reduction in time per annotation *
      - Avoid spend on manual annotation in CVAT & LabelStudio (via
      automated tooling)
      - Reduce time spent by ML team waiting to receive annotations
      - *We recently helped Standard AI
      <[LINK]>
to
      save $600k / year on annotation costs*

   - *2) Significant reduction in annotation volumes*
      - Avoid unnecessary spend on annotation via data curation (only label
      highest priority data)
      - *We helped Automotus
      <[LINK]>to
      achieve a 25% reduction in dataset size & a 33% reduction in
      annotation costs*

   - *3) Streamline data management overheads*
      - Reduce internal AI dev. costs writing custom code to manage
      training data pipelines
      - Limit effort of manual data collection (across team of 4-5 drivers)
      - Avoid administrative QA burden of AI team checking low quality
      annotations
      -
*We helped Plainsight
      <[LINK]>to
      save over 50% on AI data management costs *

Would be great to connect & discuss the specific areas of value we've
identified from our working sessions with Himanshu, Anshuman, & the wider
team - do you have time to discuss later this week or early next?

subject: Encord <> [COMPANY] Intro | Follow-up on referral from Ben [SENDER] (Motorway)
text:
Hi [NAME],

Reaching out because I met Ben [SENDER] from Motorway last week at an AI
Leaders dinner we hosted (would love to invite you to the next one we host
if it's of interest!) and he recommended I get in touch.

I work for Encord, a data development platform for computer vision AI teams
in the vehicle inspection space. We've recently onboarded Tractable to help
scale their data curation & annotation pipelines. Just like [COMPANY] they're
leveraging vision models for vehicle visual inspection use cases (damage
detection, value appraisal, etc) .

They mostly came to us due to concerns about the competitiveness of their
model quality and delivery speed as they started to scale. We've also
helped quite a few teams who've struggled with LabelBox move over - I heard
this was the case for you. We also offer a managed service for annotation
if it's of interest to teams and provide a dedicated team rather than using
crowdsourcing like others.

Given the work we're doing with the teams at Tractable and Ben's
recommendation, I thought it'd make sense for us to be introduced if it
becomes of interest. Are you open to a quick call this week? My Thursday is
wide open and Friday afternoon is looking pretty open right now.

subject: Annotation budgets [YEAR]
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Noticed that [COMPANY] has been expanding to new markets (e.g. Oil & Gas, Construction etc), and was wondering if managing annotation budgets was top of mind as you re-train ML models for these new domains?

Many Product / Data Leads of leading Robotics / AV teams we work with (inc. Physical Intelligence, Pickle Robot, and Wayve) were struggling to balance customer demand for new features with the exploding data annotation costs required to train new models.

With Encord, teams can annotate native video (vs. breaking videos down frame-by-frame) - an approach which has helped Pickle Robot to save over 60% on annual annotation costs following its transition to Encord.

Open to learning more?

subject: Encord & Ontada | Chatted to Ken
text:
Hi [NAME],

We just got off the phone with Ken, who mentioned that the team is
considering Encord and Labelbox for your data annotation and curation needs.

It sounds like this responsibility has fallen to you after Wanmei's
departure, and there is a bit of pressure to not delay further on this from
a few team members.

I understand there's short-term urgency, but in the long run, Labelbox's
ongoing shift away from being a platform-focused product to a

instability-issues Ken also highlighted.

I'd be happy to hop on a call to help you weigh the pros and cons if that
would be helpful.

subject: Woven - data curation solution
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

We've recently onboarded Woven, so thought it may make sense to reach out to see if we can help at [COMPANY] in a similar way.

Woven's Computer Vision team faced challenges with existing data curation solutions (Voxel51 & internal tools), which lacked the speed & scalability required to efficiently search through their training datasets (capping out at ~1m images).

At Encord, we've built a high-performance architecture to support indexing and searching through billions of data items (using embeddings visualisations, quality metric filters & natural language searches), enabling CV teams to avoid bottlenecks in model development.

Open to learning more?
